title: Profitability management
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point, bus-profit, only defines what profit is, while the new point teaches how to improve profit by controlling fixed and variable costs and lifting revenue, which is a different and deeper Year 12 idea.

draft.title: Profitability management
card: Profit is revenue minus expenses. A business can raise profit by cutting costs, by lifting revenue, or by doing both.
costs that stay the same however much is sold, such as rent and insurance. They can be controlled by renegotiating contracts or shifting to cheaper premises.
costs that rise and fall with output, such as materials and sales commissions. They can be controlled by finding cheaper suppliers or cutting waste.
money earned from sales, which is price multiplied by quantity sold. Marketing can lift the quantity sold, and a change in pricing can lift the amount earned on each sale.
draft.remember: Profit improves when costs are controlled, revenue is lifted, or both happen together.

a.q: Which action would control a variable cost for a bakery?
opts: Switching to a cheaper flour supplier
Renegotiating the shop lease for a lower rent
Moving the shop to a cheaper building
a.why: Flour is a material used in making bread, so its cost rises and falls with output. Rent is tempting but it stays the same however many loaves are sold, so it is a fixed cost.
a.clue: Which cost changes with the number of loaves baked?

b.q: Jade runs a gym in Bathurst. Her rent and insurance are steady, but profit is low. She runs a social media campaign that brings in more paying members. Which part of profitability management is this?
b.why: The campaign brings in more members, so the quantity sold rises and so does revenue. It is not a cost control, because the campaign does not lower the gym's rent or insurance. It is not a price change either, because the membership price has not moved.
b.clue: What did the campaign change: a cost, a price or the number of sales?

a.best: Switching to a cheaper flour supplier
